text:
maria: fyi we've been seeing a lot of jitter for small tenants because the continuous coalesce window lumps everything together. thought: add a tiny admission gate that routes tiny, latency-sensitive requests to a fastpath, gives a short warmup lane to mid-size requests (to help KV cache), otherwise defer to the normal batcher.
kevin: sounds promising. important note: gate should be admission-only. it returns ADMIT_FASTPATH | ADMIT_WARMUP | DEFER_TO_BATCHER and the scheduler acts on that. keeps separation of concerns.
maria: exactly. sketch of criteria: tokens, deadline_hint, and a per-tenant credit budget so a noisy tenant can't hog fastpath.
jamal: also consider recent kv-warmup benefit. too many fastpath hits could reduce warm cache effectiveness for longer sequences. warmup lane should preferentially pick requests that will warm KV.
erin: operationally we need a fallback if fastpath compute is saturated: downgrade to DEFER_TO_BATCHER. ops-bot should alert when fastpath util > 75%.
ops-bot: alert: fastpath_util=77% on pool-c - recommend scale or reduce fastpath credits. (auto-note)
maria: toy proto for the gate config (informal):
```
fastpath.max_tokens = 32
fastpath.rate_limit_per_tenant = 60 reqs/min
warmup.min_tokens = 33
warmup.max_tokens = 256
warmup.credit_window = 10s
warmup.credits_per_window = 3
```
This keeps fastpath tight and allows short warmup bursts.
kevin: interface details: gate should return a decision + reason tag (e.g. "over_rate", "deadline_ok", "kv_warmup_candidate"). we must emit metrics for each decision and reason.
j amal: +1 on reason tags. without them debugging is a nightmare. also expose histograms per-path: fastpath latency, warmup latency, batcher enqueue-delay.
erin: rollout: start in sim-mode for 72h (increment "would_fastpath" & "would_warmup" metrics and annotate traces but always return DEFER_TO_BATCHER). then enable real fastpath at 0.5%-2% per-box, ramp to ~10% with A/B canary tenants. include router kill-switch that can route everyone to legacy batcher.
maria: sim-mode is a must. add a sim-mode flag that flips the gate into observe-only. we'll capture CSVs of decision counts and trace samples.
kevin: config surface: default global config + tenant-class overrides (free/paid/enterprise) and a tiny opt-in flag for specific latency-sensitive SKUs. avoid per-tenant config explosion.
jamal: testing: replay last week's traffic into the sim-mode gate and measure KV-hit delta and tail latency. run microbench of fastpath to ensure low p99. also add chaos test where fastpath pool is artificially saturated to verify downgrade path.
erin: monitoring: ops-bot to emit alerts for fastpath saturation and delta in KV-hit-rate vs baseline. make sure rollback is cheap.
maria: long-term idea: replace deterministic thresholds with a small decision function that predicts tail impact, but we should ship deterministic admission first for auditability.
kevin: docs needed: admission contract page (enums, reason labels, config knobs, telemetry keys). expose decision ID in traces for correlation.
jamal: also add a weekly job to surface sim-mode trace samples to the RFC authors during rollout.
erin: next steps: maria writes RFC with enums, proto, rollout plan, and sim-mode results. kevin/jamal to run sims and share CSVs. i'll wire ops-bot alerts to canary pipelines.
maria: i'll get the RFC draft and sim CSV attached by EOD Friday. thanks everyone :rocket:
